NATS 2.15 docs: a leaf node is 'a NATS server that opens an outbound connection to a remote NATS system' and needs 'no inbound firewall rule, no public address' on its side; leaf links compose into trees (a leaf can be a hub for leaves further out, and can dial several hubs); isolation comes from account binding: 'Bound to its own account, only the subjects that account imports and exports cross the link', while the default account has 'no subject boundary'

NATS 2.15 super-cluster docs: a gateway 'joins one cluster to another cluster'; each server opens one gateway connection to each other cluster; messages cross only when the remote cluster has interest. The leafnodes page adds that 'A gateway joins two clusters that can both accept connections from each other', unlike a leaf node, which dials out

NATS 2.15 docs: nats-server implements MQTT v3.1.1 only (a v5 client is refused at CONNECT with return code 1), supports QoS 0, 1 and 2 (QoS 2 since 2.10), stores MQTT sessions and retained messages in JetStream, and maps MQTT topic levels to NATS subject tokens ('/' becomes '.'); Sparkplug B is not mentioned

Eclipse Sparkplug 3.0 (dated 2022-10-21, EPL-2.0) defines an MQTT topic namespace, payload and session state; topics are namespace/group_id/message_type/edge_node_id/[device_id] with namespace spBv1.0 and message types NBIRTH/NDEATH/NDATA/NCMD, DBIRTH/DDEATH/DDATA/DCMD and STATE; host and edge applications may use MQTT v3.1.1 or v5.0

Headscale README at v0.29.7: its goal 'is to provide self-hosters and hobbyists with an open-source server'; it 'implements a narrow scope, a single Tailscale network (tailnet), suitable for a personal use, or a small open-source organisation'

Eclipse Zenoh 1.10.2 README: 'Zero Overhead Pub/Sub, Store/Query and Compute' that 'unifies data in motion, data at rest, and computations'; the Rust crate is the reference implementation and zenoh-pico is a pure-C implementation for constrained devices; licence Apache-2.0 or EPL-2.0 (C-LIC-051)
